sentences.text: Iguanodon is a genus of iguanodontian dinosaurs that was named in 1825.
This animal was a large, bulky herbivore reaching up to 9 to 11 meters in length and weighing 4.5 metric tons.
It possessed large thumb spikes possibly used for defense and long prehensile fifth fingers used for foraging.
Numerous specimens, including nearly complete skeletons from two bone beds, have allowed researchers to form hypotheses about the feeding, movement, and social behavior of Iguanodon.
Research indicates that Iguanodon had a straight tail and back, walking with its body held horizontally, rather than the bent tail previously reconstructed.
Due to deeply inset tooth rows and other anatomical details, it is believed that Iguanodon had a cheek-like structure to retain food in the mouth.
The genus Iguanodon was described by Gideon Mantell in 1825.
Mantell named the genus based on fossil specimens found in England.
Iguanodon was the second dinosaur formally named based on fossil specimens, following Megalosaurus.
A popular legend suggests Mary Ann Mantell discovered the first Iguanodon teeth in Tilgate Forest in 1822, though there is no evidence she accompanied her husband.
A find in Nehden, Germany, included at least 15 individuals ranging from 2 to 8 meters in length, comprising both Mantellisaurus and Iguanodon bernissartensis.
Evidence suggests Iguanodon lived in groups, as a find in Germany indicates the animals were killed together by flash floods.
Iguanodon bernissartensis is the type species of the genus Iguanodon.
Iguanodon belongs to the larger group Iguanodontia, which also includes duck-billed hadrosaurs.
I. anglicus, described by Holl in 1829, is considered a nomen dubium, while I. galvensis was named by Verdú et al. in 2015.
Delapparentia turolensis, described by Ruiz-Omeñaca in 2011, is listed as a synonym of Iguanodon.
The type species Iguanodon bernissartensis lived during the Barremian age of the Early Cretaceous.
Many species historically classified in the genus Iguanodon date from the Late Jurassic to the Early Cretaceous.
Iguanodon bernissartensis lived in Belgium, Germany, Spain, and possibly England between 126 and 122 million years ago during the Barremian to early Aptian ages.
Iguanodon lived during the early Early Cretaceous period, between 126 and 120 million years ago (Barremian to Aptian stages).
It is debated whether remains previously referred to as Iguanodon in England belong to I. bernissartensis or to other genera like Mantellisaurus, Barilium, and Hypselospinus.
Louis Dollo proposed that Iguanodon should be modeled after a cassowary or wallaby with the thumb spike on the thumb rather than the nose, a view that later prevailed but was eventually discounted.
It is debated whether Dollo's reconstruction of Iguanodon was correct, specifically regarding the bend he introduced into the tail which contradicted fossil evidence.

Jack Horner once proposed that hadrosaurids formed two distinct groups with Iguanodon on the line to flat-headed hadrosaurines and Ouranosaurus on the line to crested lambeosaurines, but this proposal was rejected.
